title: Ward v0.1 P0: local developer preview
description: Parent for the P0 scope in WARD_MVP_AGENT_SPEC.md §5. Organizes scope only; ordering lives on the subtasks' dependencies. Release is gated on every mandatory P0 gate (spec §14) passing on macOS.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/security-tests.md maps T01-T26 to a test and a recorded result, with mocks vs real packaged components distinguished

implementationNotes: Handoff, 2026-09-28, session renewal on context budget (opum-agent watchdog); not a decision stop. Live state, verified by quest task list and gh: no task In Progress (scope.otherRefsRead true, no unseen ids), no open PRs, main = dev = 860c18d (promoted through PR #4; tree-equal and ancestry assertions passed). Done: WCLI-2 scaffold (PR #1), WCLI-17 CI (PR #2), WCLI-18 profile records ruleset 24097150 (PR #3). Ready now: WCLI-3 ADRs, WCLI-4 crypto envelope, WCLI-16 launcher hardening. WCLI-16 blocks WCLI-5 (setup) and WCLI-8 (secrets) because launching through bun loads the working directory's bunfig.toml and .env first (see WCLI-2 notes). Recommended order: WCLI-16 or WCLI-4 first. WCLI-3 carries the design questions opum-agent records in opum-doc (vault format, keychain binding, plugin name); argue them there. Method notes for the successor: (1) dev has a required-checks ruleset, so every change, tracker-only included, lands by PR; a tracker note needs its own chore branch. (2) File new tasks on the branch that will deliver them: records filed inside a feature branch stay invisible to siblings until it merges (WCLI-2 cost a round of waiting). (3) `gh api --jq` rejects --argjson and returns empty, so a gate loop built on it silently never concludes; use python over saved JSON (this bit the first promotion gate check, caught before the push). (4) Spec §15 wants an independent review of crypto, error paths, authority checks and the keychain boundary: dispatch the opum-workflow reviewer agent per security PR, as on PR #1. (5) This session's auto-mode classifier refused the first gh pr merge as 'merge without review'; the user then approved merges with 'proceed'. A successor should confirm merge authority with its own user rather than inherit this. Skills: opum-sdlc (task before branch, promotion), opum-handoff restore, quest, lore.

Confirm merge authority with your own user before merging. Start with the opum-handoff skill in restore mode, then opum-sdlc.

Recycle handoff, 2026-09-28, written at the orchestrator's recycle request (context over the fleet budget). This is not a decision stop. Verified live just now: quest task list --status 'In Progress' is empty (scope.otherRefsRead true, unseenTaskIds empty); gh pr list --state open is empty; origin/main == origin/dev == c41a62a (promotion #17; trees equal and ancestry asserted after the push). DONE this session: WCLI-16 launcher hardening (#8); WCLI-4 envelope (#10); WCLI-3 ADRs 0001-0003 (#12, opum-doc ODOC-312); WCLI-5 KeyProvider and Keychain adapter (#15); WCLI-23 ADR 0004 platform target (#16, ODOC-316); WCLI-21 and WCLI-22 filed (#14). NEXT, in the orchestrator's order: WCLI-6 (encrypted SQLite snapshot store), then WCLI-20 (ward setup, which depends on WCLI-5 and WCLI-6). WCLI-20's notes carry the obligations from the WCLI-5 review: serialize setup, for example with a lock file in ~/.ward, because KeyProvider.create is check-then-write; resolve vault_key_write_unconfirmed with load() and never rewrite; exit explicitly after vault_key_unavailable, because a pending native call can keep the process alive; never zero a key buffer on a timed-out write path. WCLI-19 (BUN_OPTIONS, BUN_BE_BUN) is an accepted P0 limit pending opum-agent OPAG-672 (Developer ID signing, an operator decision). METHOD NOTES for the successor: (1) Merge authority is not inherited. My user granted it for this session only, so ask your own user before the first gh pr merge. (2) Every real-Keychain write needs the user's explicit authorisation at the time. The orchestrator cannot give it. Probe namespace opum.ward.probe-* only, never opum.ward or ~/.ward. test/qualification/keychain-roundtrip.ts refuses without WARD_QUALIFY_REAL_KEYCHAIN=1. (3) Tests: the @napi-rs/keyring mock (test/support/no-real-keychain.ts) must be the FIRST import (a bare side-effect import) of any test that reaches src/adapters, because bunfig.toml's preload applies only from the repository root. test/test-isolation.test.ts enforces this. 'biome check --write' reorders named imports, so use 'biome format --write'. (4) Dispatch the opum-workflow reviewer per security PR (spec §15), and have it verify its own findings after the fixes. Both WCLI-5 passes found real defects. (5) Gate merges with a gate script that checks EVERY run of Check, Docs and Tracker integrity on the exact head SHA, and re-check the head SHA before merging. (6) Design questions go to opum-agent with a recommendation and a measurement. It decides, opum-doc records, and the ADR cites the ODOC id. (7) In zsh, a $VAR holding several flags is not word-split, so pass quest actor flags through a shell function. Skills to load: opum-handoff restore, opum-sdlc, quest, lore.

Recycle handoff, 2026-09-28, written after the orchestrator's recycle request (context over the fleet budget); supersedes nothing in the earlier notes on this task, which still stand. State, verified live just now by git rev-parse and quest task list: origin/main == origin/dev == 9709d91 (WCLI-20's squash, promoted through PR #22; post-push assertions held), no task In Progress on dev (scope read), no uncommitted work beyond this note. DONE this session: WCLI-6 encrypted SQLite snapshot store (#19) and WCLI-20 ward setup (#21), each landed with its acceptance criteria checked in the PR, each independently reviewed (spec §15; WCLI-6 four rounds, WCLI-20 five rounds — one HIGH found and fixed in each: the foreign-WAL mutation on refusal, and the pid-lock mutual-exclusion race that prompted the flock(2)-via-bun:ffi redesign). NEXT for the successor: WCLI-24 (provision the four .lore/agents/ profiles) — PR #23 carries its full brief on the task record. METHOD NOTES: (1) Merge authority is not inherited: my user granted it per PR this session, so ask your own user before the first gh pr merge. (2) Never pipe a quest write through head/tail: this session lost a note to an early-closed pipe exactly the way the WCLI-1 notes warn; verify writes with quest task view, unpiped. (3) opum-workflow's guard hook refuses git commit while HEAD is dev — keep tracker writes and branch/commit in separate Bash calls. (4) Until WCLI-24 lands, the opum-workflow reviewer specialist refuses dispatch (missing lore review profile); dispatch a general-purpose reviewer with the same adversarial brief instead. (5) The setup lock is flock(2) on darwin with an O_EXCL pid fallback whose check-then-delete race is WCLI-21/22's qualification precondition (measured 12 pairs in 20 rounds). (6) CI Check runs on Linux ARM64 self-hosted runners — keep tests platform-aware, since the fallback path only runs there. Skills: opum-handoff restore, opum-sdlc, quest, lore.
